In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of ASPL in type-I and II Al/sub x/Gasub 1-x/ As /InGaP HJ structures.
the ASPL phenomena in AlGaAs/InGaAs HJs and InGaAs/InP QWs.
the investigation of the up-conversion luminescence of infrared to red in Al/sub x/GaxAs/InGaAs HJ and InGaAs/Al/sub x/GaxP QW structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the ASPL process in HJs and QWs, the mechanism is the same as that in bulk semiconducting crystals, i.e. the phonon-assisted up-conversion, but the efficiency is greatly increased due to the presence of a potential barrier which confines the electron-hole pairs in the active region of the heterostructure.
the up-conversion in HJs and QWs has been observed in a number of systems and the up-conversion mechanism is different from that of the bulk semiconducting materials.
the ASPL phenomena are not observed in type-I HJs and QWs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ASPL phenomenon in HJs and QWs can be understood in terms of the carrier transfer process between the conduction bands of the two semiconductors forming the HJ or the QW.
the up-conversion phenomena are observed not only in type-I HJs and QWs, but also in type-II HJs.
ASPL is observed in HJs and QWs with a type-I band alignment, and that the ASPL intensity is enhanced in HJs with a type-II band alignment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ASPL phenomena in type-I and -II Al/sub x/Gasub 1-x/ As/InGaP HJs can be understood in terms of the band-to-band transitions in the HJ region.
the type-II HJ structure is more efficient than the type-I HJ structure in up-converting the infrared (IR) light to red light.
we have demonstrated the ASPL phenomena in both type-I and type-I/II heterojunctions and quantum wells.
